newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canada '97 pork exports to Japan can rise - chief.
newsitem.headline: Canada '97 pork exports to Japan can rise - chief.

text.p: Canadian pork exports to Japan will rise to about 60,000 tonnes in 1997 if Japan lifts its emergency tariffs on the meat, the head of the Canadian pork industry trade group said.

"We don't have big volume available, but our pork quality is better than the United States and Taiwan. Pork exports to Japan next year will rise to around 60,000 tonnes if Japan lifts the tariffs," Jim Morris, president of Canada Pork International, told Reuters in an interview.
Morris is currently visiting Tokyo with meat industry officials to promote exports to the Japanese market.
Canada exported 341,058 tonnes of pork in 1995, according to the CPI. Japan was the second-largest market, following the United States, with 48,267 tonnes.
Japan is one of the world's largest pork importers, buying mainly from the United States and Taiwan.

The Japanese government imposed emergency tariffs on imported pork from this July to protect local producers from an influx of imports. The tariff is to remain until March 1997. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk (81-3-3432-7391)
